analysis:
Examined the new `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens` policy (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift head lines 61-78) and its wiring into the scheduler config (EngineV2Factory+Production.swift head lines 310-311), plus the live test update (Qwen35CheckpointRetentionLiveTests.swift).

The policy is tightly gated. It applies only to the paged backend, only to dense Qwen35 (via `isDenseQwen35`, which is defined outside the supplied evidence), and only when the store is an `SSDHybridCheckpointStore` using the paged or native-quantized paged layout. It returns the store's existing `minEffectiveTokens` floor, so no floor is lowered. It is not gated on `constructionPurpose`, unlike the benchmark-only recurrent policy. The serving path therefore gets an additional end-of-prompt checkpoint boundary for dense Qwen.

Security relevance (T-041, TB-007) is limited to cache-persistence behavior. An extra checkpoint near the prompt end is written through the existing SSD store, which keeps the HMAC-keyed names, AES-GCM encryption, 30-minute TTL, salt scoping, and disk budget and guards. This PR does not change these controls, add a new at-rest artifact kind, or add metadata fields. The effect is more or deeper checkpoints per donation for dense Qwen, meaning slightly more disk write volume and a marginally richer same-account TTFT hit/miss oracle. Both stay within the accepted SEC-035 posture. Whether the new boundary stays within the endurance and benefit-floor guards depends on SDK `CBv2SchedulerConfig` behavior, which is not supplied.

The test change only adjusts expected positions and adds a geometry assertion; it has no production impact.

Unverified contracts: the SDK's handling of `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens` and `demandedLatestPromptEndMarginTokens`, the `isDenseQwen35` definition, and whether the added checkpoint passes the per-donation gate in SSDPrefixCache.donate. No regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
